title: Chars
recap: A char stores one character and character literals use single quotes. Printing a char displays its character representation rather than an integer value.
Escape sequences begin with a backslash. Common examples include newline, tab, escaped single quote, escaped double quote, and escaped backslash.
objectives: Initialize and print a single char value.
Use escaped quotes around a character in output.
Use escaped backslashes in a path literal.
Use tab and newline character escape sequences deliberately.
warnings: A character literal uses single quotes and must represent one character or escape sequence.
Escape sequences use a backslash, not a forward slash.
Do not use implementation-defined multicharacter literals.
challenge: Repair the badge display while retaining char marker initialized to 'K'. Print the marker inside single quotes, print the literal path C:\lab\chapter4 using escaped backslashes, and separate column characters A and B with one tab escape. End every report line with a newline and match the exact deterministic output.
hints: The single-quote character can be represented by the escape sequence '\''.
Each literal backslash in output requires two backslashes in a string literal.
Print 'A', then '\t', then 'B' before the final newline.
